notes.title: Original PDF
notes.html:
The problem as given on DomJudge:

prob-Triplet.pdf

The PDF's example outputs are wrong: Example 1 (nums1 = [2,0,1,3,4], nums2 = [0,1,2,3,4]) has 5 good triplets, not 4: it misses (0, 1, 3). Example 2 says n = 4 but lists 5 numbers; with [4,0,1,3,2] and [4,1,0,2,3] the answer is 4 (as on LeetCode), not 0.

notes.title: Teacher's solution
notes.html:
Relabel each value by its position in nums1, so nums2 becomes P[i] = pos1[nums2[i]]. A good triplet is then i < j < k with P[i] < P[j] < P[k].

For each middle index j: leftLess[j] = #{i < j : P[i] < P[j]} and rightGreater[j] = #{k > j : P[k] > P[j]}. The answer is the sum over j of leftLess[j] × rightGreater[j].

Both counts come from a Fenwick tree (BIT) over values.

Time: O(n log n) · Space: O(n)
